concepts.title: Mahābhārata as a Mokṣa Śāstra
concepts.description: Mahābhārata is fundamentally a sacred text that aims at Mokṣa, and concentrating only on social, sociological, or ethnological aspects misses out on its core value.

concepts.title: Divine Presence in Mahābhārata
concepts.description: Embarking on the journey of Mahābhārata is experiencing the physical presence of the divine in our life through accounts of Kṛṣṇa, Vyāsa, Bhārgavarāma, Balarāmā, Bhīṣma, and Animāndavyā.

concepts.title: Birth Omens of Pāṇḍavas and Duryodhana
concepts.description: When the Pāṇḍavas are born, devas appear in the sky and shower blessings and flowers, whereas when Duryodhana is born, a donkey brays, prompting a minister to suggest abandoning him.

concepts.title: Animāndavyā Muni's Torture
concepts.description: Animāndavyā Muni is mistakenly caught as a thief and punished with a spear to the spine without dying, living out his life with the spear still intact.

concepts.title: Animāndavyā Cursing Yamadeva
concepts.description: Animāndavyā curses Yamadeva for misinterpreting Dharma, proving that even Dharmadeva himself is not above Dharma.

concepts.title: Churning Heart and Mind for Dharma
concepts.description: Mahābhārata presents complex logic, decisions, contexts, and emotions that force a student to grind and churn their heart and mind to earn an understanding of Dharma.

concepts.title: Devavrata's Spontaneous Pratijñā
concepts.description: In Ādi Parva, Devavrata spontaneously decides and proclaims the Bhīṣma-Pratijñā to satisfy his father Śantanu's kāma, becoming Bhīṣma.

concepts.title: Conditions for Śantanu and Satyavatī's Marriage
concepts.description: To marry Satyavatī, Śantanu must fulfill Satyavatī's father's condition that her son become the next king, a proposal initially rejected by Śantanu.

concepts.title: Bhīṣma's Vow of Brahmacarya
concepts.description: Devavrata accepts Satyavatī's father's conditions without consultation, takes a lifelong vow of Brahmacarya, renounces his claim to the throne, and earns the power to choose his time of death.

concepts.title: Questions on Bhīṣma's Decision
concepts.description: As Yuvarāja, Devavrata's decision to renounce administration without consulting his father or considering the kingdom's impact raises questions about its Dharma.

concepts.title: Irony of Satyavatī's Sons
concepts.description: Satyavatī's two sons both passed away without having any children, leaving the younger son Vicitravīrya's widows, Ambikā and Ambālikā, heirless.

concepts.title: Satyavatī's Proposal to Bhīṣma
concepts.description: Satyavatī asks Bhīṣma to break his vow, take the throne, and father children with the widows via surrogate tradition, but Bhīṣma rejects both proposals.

concepts.title: Birth of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu, and Vidura
concepts.description: Maharṣi Vyāsa fathers children with the widows and a maid, leading to the birth of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu, and Vidura.

concepts.title: Kingdom Unseated and War
concepts.description: Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Pāṇḍu were unfit to rule, Vidura could not be king due to his birth, Pāṇḍu died too soon, and Yudhiṣṭira was unseated by Duryodhana, ultimately leading to the Kurukṣetra war where 18 akṣauhiṇīs died.

concepts.title: Bhīṣma as the Brahmacarya Archetype
concepts.description: Bhīṣma stands as the ultimate Brahmacarya archetype of Mahābhārata, contrasting with Arjuna's inability to keep his 12-year brahmacarya and his father's weakness for Gaṅgādevī and Satyavatī.

concepts.title: Bhīṣma Rendered Powerless
concepts.description: Bound by his Pratijñā, Bhīṣma became powerless even before a blind king and his son, missing an opportunity to lead Bhāratavarṣa.

concepts.title: Gāndhārī's Lineage
concepts.description: Gāndhārī was the daughter of King Subala from Gandhāradeśa, and her eldest brother was Śakuni.

concepts.title: Arranged Marriage to Dhṛtarāṣṭra
concepts.description: Bhīṣma sends a messenger to King Subala for Gāndhārī's hand in marriage to Dhṛtarāṣṭra; Subala hesitates due to the prince's blindness but agrees due to the Kurus' greatness.

concepts.title: Gāndhārī's Blindfold Pratijñā
concepts.description: Upon hearing her husband is blind, Gāndhārī blindfolds herself with a cloth to never experience more than her husband, choosing to stand behind him in every sense.

concepts.title: Repercussions of Gāndhārī's Blindfold
concepts.description: Gāndhārī's hasty Pratijñā contributed to improper parenting, leaving Duryodhana's ego uncorrected, and metaphorically symbolized turning a blind eye to her sons' adharma.

concepts.title: The Power of Motherhood
concepts.description: Amma notes that motherhood is as vast as the universe, and a woman can influence the entire world with it, whereas Gāndhārī failed to influence her children due to an emotional response.

concepts.title: Arjuna's Pratijñā to Kill Jayadratha
concepts.description: Arjuna pledges to kill Jayadratha before sunset on the day following Abhimanyu's death in the Cakravyūha.

concepts.title: Abhimanyu's Death
concepts.description: Abhimanyu breaches Droṇācārya's Cakravyūha alone due to Jayadratha's interference blocking the Pāṇḍavas, and is simultaneously attacked and killed by multiple Kaurava warriors, breaking Dharmayuddha ethics.

concepts.title: Kṛṣṇa's Intervention for Arjuna
concepts.description: When Kaurava military formations protect Jayadratha and hide him behind Droṇācārya, Kṛṣṇa uses his Sudarśanachakra to mask the sun, creating an illusion of sunset so Jayadratha exposes himself.

concepts.title: Fulfillment of Arjuna's Vow
concepts.description: After Kṛṣṇa reveals the sun, Arjuna takes up his Gāṇḍīva and kills Jayadratha with the Pāśupatāstra, saving his Pratijñā from failure.

concepts.title: The Rigged Game of Dice
concepts.description: Duryodhana invites the Pāṇḍavas to a game of dice influenced by Śakuni, where Yudhiṣṭhira loses his army, kingdom, brothers, himself, and Draupadī.

concepts.title: Draupadī's Humiliation and Bhīma's Vows
concepts.description: As Duhśāsana attempts to disrobe Draupadī, and Duryodhana invites her to sit on his thigh, an enraged Bhīma vows to tear open Duhśāsana's chest to drink his blood and to break Duryodhana's thigh.

concepts.title: Bhīma Approves Peace
concepts.description: In Udyoga Parva, despite his fierce vows, Bhīma approves of peace over war when Kṛṣṇa goes as a peace messenger, showing he was willing to forgo his Pratijñās for the greater good.

concepts.title: Fulfillment of Bhīma's Vows
concepts.description: Bhīma kills Duhśāsana without conflicting Dharma and later breaks Duryodhana's thigh during a mace fight following Kṛṣṇa's instruction, perfectly aligning his actions with dharma.

concepts.title: Daily Life Pratijñās
concepts.description: People make emotional vows in daily life, such as giving silent treatments or vowing not to speak to someone, which mirror impulsive Pratijñās.

concepts.title: Contemplation Questions for Vows
concepts.description: Two questions for personal vows are whether it arose from intellectual clarity or emotional outburst, and whether clinging to it remains beneficial to society.

concepts.title: Kṛṣṇa's Vow of Non-Violence
concepts.description: Bhagavān Śrī Kṛṣṇa vows not to take up arms in the Kurukṣetra war, offering his army to Duryodhana while joining Arjuna's side unarmed.

concepts.title: Kṛṣṇa Breaking His Vow for Dharma
concepts.description: Driven by Bhīṣma's fierce counter vow and Arjuna's hesitation, Kṛṣṇa breaks his vow, grabs a chariot wheel, and rushes towards Bhīṣma to protect Dharma.

concepts.title: Kṛṣṇa as the Pratijñā Archetype
concepts.description: Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa acts as the true Pratijñā archetype, unhindered by rigid vows and fully responsive to the call of Dharma, unlike Bhīṣma who trapped himself.

concepts.title: Karṇa's Complex Character
concepts.description: Karṇa epitomizes the confluence of right and wrong, and his story is debated with various literary versions like Bhāsa's Karṇabhāram and Śivajī Sawanth's Mṛtyunjaya.
concepts.section: KARṆA: THE MAESTRO WHO WENT WIDE OF THE MARK
